body: Cases: Novo Nordisk (GLP-1 pioneer; Europe's most valuable company June 2024, then -73% to below pre-Wegovy levels by Feb 2026), Eli Lilly (fast follower with a better molecule; first $1tn drugmaker Nov 2025, ~63% of US branded obesity scripts), Monster (created a category and kept it), Celsius (new sub-category, 60x then -73%), Tesla (EVs; 35x then -73%), Nvidia (AI compute; see case_study:nvidia). Pattern: (1) the up-move begins when demand visibly exceeds supply (Wegovy shortages 2021-23, Model 3 waitlists, Pepsi DSD shelf space) — the signal is scarcity; (2) peak valuation tends to coincide with peak scarcity, exactly when competitors and capacity are arriving; (3) the winner is the player with the best head-to-head data/product and manufacturing/distribution scale (Lilly's SURPASS-2 and capacity spend; Monster's distribution system), not the first mover; (4) price normalisation (US government drug-price deals, compounding, EV price cuts) compresses margins at the same time as share loss. Early warning for the incumbent: a public head-to-head trial or benchmark that shows a superior rival, and its own next-gen product underwhelming (CagriSema Dec 2024). Lesson: in a new category, re-underwrite on competitive data every year; scarcity premiums are temporary.

data.signal_down: superior rival data; own next-gen miss; price normalisation

title: Category creation (GLP-1-type): the pioneer does not automatically win
